subject: E-Commerce
title: Central Bank Digital Currencies
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Central Bank Digital Currencies.

hook.text: 130 countries are exploring digital versions of their currencies. China already launched the digital yuan.

buildup.text: CBDCs are government-issued digital money. Unlike crypto, they're centrally controlled and backed by the state.

discovery.text: CBDCs could make payments instant and free, eliminating the need for card networks entirely.

twist.text: Privacy advocates warn CBDCs let governments track every transaction. Digital cash could mean no privacy at all.

climax.text: CBDCs could replace card networks or coexist with them. The outcome depends on privacy design choices.

punchline.text: 130 countries exploring. Digital government money: faster, cheaper, watched.

quiz.question: What is the main privacy concern about CBDCs?
options: Governments could track every single transaction
